note.note:
Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Arrange urgent EMS transport now; ambulance team will apply 12-lead ECG and determine destination hospital based on ECG findings; patient access arrangements (front door open) to ensure safe handoff.
- The clinician will remain on the line to coordinate; hand over to ambulance team upon arrival and provide pertinent history (HPI, risk factors, aspirin allergy) to ED.
- Document and communicate the aspirin allergy to the receiving hospital; consider antiplatelet therapy decisions with ED based on allergy status (aspirin may be considered per hospital protocol, but information to be relayed clearly).
- The patient understands that ACS is the priority to exclude and that ED evaluation with ECG will guide next steps.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Chest pressure described as “like someone sitting on my chest,” started a couple of hours ago while gardening; ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis (sweating), shortness of breath, and palpitations (heart feels faster).
- Onset/duration: Began during light activity (gardening); persistent for several hours.
- Radiation: Diffuse chest pain, primarily to left arm and shoulder.
- Exertion: Not during heavy activity; gardening was the trigger.
- Medical history: Hypertension; overweight; smoker (10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years); family history of heart disease (father died of heart attack around age 60; mother with heart problems); not diabetic.
- Medications: Not specified.
- Allergies: Aspirin allergy (mild swelling; not life-threatening).
- Social: Lives alone; works as a sushi restaurant owner.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints/week.
- ROS/other: Palpitations noted; stress reported; no prior similar symptoms.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Ambulance arrival and ECG planned; no labs/imaging results available at this time.
- Front door currently open; patient in private setting; patient able to speak with physician.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) – high likelihood
- Assessment / likely diagnosis (from transcript and DDx): Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI) is the leading concern given chest pressure with left arm/shoulder radiation, diaphoresis, dyspnea, and palpitations in a patient with significant risk factors (hypertension, smoking, obesity, positive family history). Onset during light activity does not exclude ACS; ambulance ECG is planned.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript/DDx):
  - Musculoskeletal chest wall pain / costochondritis – Medium likelihood
  - Aortic dissection – Low likelihood
  - Pulmonary embolism – Low likelihood
  - Other inflammatory/viral etiologies (pericarditis/myocarditis) – possible but less likely with current history
  - Other cardiac etiologies or less likely causes per DDx (valvular disease, coronary anomalies, Kounis syndrome, etc.) – acknowledged per DDx
- Investigations planned: 12-lead ECG by ambulance; ED/hospital-based workup (troponin, imaging, and further ACS workup) as dictated by ECG and clinical status.
- Treatment planned: Immediate ACS protocol to be determined by EMS/hospital; aspirin therapy to be considered by ED given aspirin allergy (patient reports allergy with swelling); hospital communication to tailor antiplatelet therapy accordingly.
- Referrals: To be determined by ED based on ACS evaluation; patient will be transferred to an appropriate hospital after ECG.

2) Musculoskeletal chest wall pain (less likely but possible)
- Assessment: Chest wall pain related to gardening activity; diffuse chest pain could reflect musculoskeletal strain.
- Differential diagnosis: Musculoskeletal chest wall pain / costochondritis (Medium); other cardiac etiologies remain higher priority.
- Investigations planned: As above (ECG first; further workup if indicated).
- Treatment planned: Not initiated in the field; ED evaluation will guide management.
- Referrals: No specialty referral at this time; ED follow-up as indicated.

Quality checks (document_healthcare_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs, physical examination findings, and baseline medications reconciliation are not provided in the transcript.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified; DDx aligns with presented symptoms and risk factors.
- Transcript quality: Conversation is coherent; essential history and red flags are captured; no major inaudible sections.

Notes:
- The patient has an aspirin allergy (mild reaction with swelling). This information will be communicated to the ED, and antiplatelet therapy will be guided by hospital protocol. There is acknowledgment from the physician that aspirin may still be considered despite the reported allergy, depending on the clinical scenario.

End of note.
